title: Putin and Pezeshkian call out US dominance ahead of BRICS - Remotestake market desk
text:
The presidents of Iran and Russia have criticised US dollar dominance ahead of the BRICS summit in India.

The Kremlin and the Iranian presidency have chosen their pre-summit posture with care. By framing the BRICS gathering in India as a platform to challenge US dollar dominance, Putin and Pezeshkian are not merely stating a preference; they are signaling a coordinated stance designed to shape the narrative before the formal sessions begin.

For Moscow, the dollar critique is a familiar instrument. It reinforces the broader theme of a multipolar world order that Russia has advanced since the onset of Western sanctions. For Tehran, the message serves a dual purpose: aligning with a powerful partner while appealing to other BRICS members who harbor their own reservations about the greenback's reach.

The timing is deliberate. Announcing the criticism ahead of the summit, rather than during it, allows both leaders to set expectations and test the waters among their peers. It also ensures the media cycle is dominated by their chosen issue, crowding out questions about internal BRICS disagreements or the practical difficulties of de-dollarization.

Yet the gap between rhetoric and reality remains wide. BRICS members have divergent economic interests, and the dollar's role in global trade and finance is not easily displaced. The statements from Putin and Pezeshkian are best understood as political positioning, not a concrete policy shift.

For observers, the real story is not the criticism itself but the choreography around it. The summit will likely produce more symbolic declarations than structural change, but the signal is clear: the bloc's leading voices intend to keep the dollar question at the center of their collective agenda.
